To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the growth inhibitory activities of anthocyanins and their degradation products are strongly affected by the experimental conditions, in particular the presence of hydrogen peroxide and the limited stability of the phenolic acids.

the phenolic degradation products of the tested anthocyanidin do not contribute to their growth inhibitory properties and that hydrogen peroxide might generate experimental artefact in the assessment of growth inhibitory properties.
the degradation of the anthocyanidin DEL generates the phenolic acid GA.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a potential artefact of anthocyanin studies in cell culture.
the degradation of the anthocyanidin DEL in cell culture medium.
a possible artefact, i.e. hydrogen peroxide formation, that might affect the growth inhibiting properties of the tested anthocyanidin derivatives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the growth inhibitory potential of DEL is limited by its instability and by its ability to generate hydrogen peroxide.
the growth inhibitory property of DEL is not based on its degradation product GA, but is most likely a direct effect of DEL itself.
the growth inhibitory property of anthocyanins might be attributed to the parent anthocyanidin, but the contribution of degradation products cannot be excluded.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the degradation products of the anthocyanidin DEL are not responsible for the growth inhibitory activity of DEL.
DEL is not a good choice for cell culture experiments due to its rapid degradation.
DEL is a promising compound with respect to its biological properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the degradation products of anthocyanids should be considered when studying their effects in vitro.
the growth inhibitory activity of DEL is not caused by GA, but rather by the generation of hydrogen peroxide during the degradation of DEL.
the formation of hydrogen per oxide by anthocyanidin and GA treatment should be taken into account when studying the effects of these compounds.
